standard_prerequisites.name: The description of the sections with support in a specialization-stable subset as the filtered colimit of the sections with support in the closed subsets it contains
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Author lemma lemma-adjoint-ext, whose statement is reproduced verbatim as a context span of this card (source lines 996-1004)
standard_prerequisites.use: Combined with the commutativity of directed colimits with direct sums, gives that the functor commutes with direct sums so that the map may be checked on shifts of the ring.

standard_prerequisites.name: K-flat complexes as a model for the derived tensor product and the total complex of a double complex
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used at the start of the counted proof (source lines 1180-1184)
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides the explicit representative of the derived tensor product on which the canonical map is built.

standard_prerequisites.name: The reduction of an isomorphism of functors commuting with direct sums to the shifts of the ring
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Invoked inside the counted proof at source lines 1196-1198 as a cross-chapter pointer
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the verification of the displayed identity to the case of a shift of the ring, where it is immediate.

core_obligations: Represent both sides: the proof lets J^\bullet be a complex in the category of modules supported in T representing the derived sections of the structure sheaf, and represents the given complex by a K-flat complex, so that the derived tensor product is the total complex of the double complex, which still has support in T (proof lines 1180-1184)

Build the canonical map: from the map of the derived sections to the structure sheaf the proof obtains a map to the given complex, and by the adjointness property of the functor obtains the displayed canonical map factoring it (proof lines 1184-1190)

Check the map on generators: the functor commutes with direct sums, by the colimit description of the support functor together with the commutativity of directed colimits with direct sums and the corresponding property of the classical local cohomology, and a cross-chapter reduction then shows that it suffices to test the map on shifts of the ring, where it is clear (proof lines 1190-1198)
The multiplicative statements: the remaining identities and the assertion about the support of the derived tensor product follow by transitivity of derived tensor products (proof lines 1200-1202)
proof_roadmap: 取 J^∙ ∈ Mod_{A,T} 表示 RΓ_T(A)，取 K-平坦复形 K^∙ 表示 K，则 RΓ_T(A) ⊗^L_A K 由 Tot(J^∙ ⊗ K^∙) 表示且各项支撑在 T；由 RΓ_T(A) → A 与伴随性得到典范映射 RΓ_T(A) ⊗^L_A K → RΓ_T(K)。
RΓ_T 与直和交换（用 lemma-adjoint-ext 的 colim 描述 + 有向 colim 与直和交换 + 经典局部上同调与直和交换），故跨章引理把验证化归到 K = A[k]，此时显然；其余恒等式与支撑断言由导出张量积的传递性得到。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement computes the derived sections with support of an arbitrary complex as the derived tensor product with the derived sections of the structure sheaf, and lists the resulting identities for a derived tensor product of two complexes together with the statement that the tensor product of two complexes supported in T is again supported in T, all under the hypothesis that the ring has finite dimension (author lemma at source lines 1162-1177, label lemma-torsion-tensor-product). The proof (source lines 1179-1203) represents both sides by explicit complexes, constructs the canonical map through the adjointness property, and then reduces the verification to shifts of the ring by combining the colimit description of the functor with the fact that it commutes with direct sums (proof lines 1190-1198); the remaining identities are formal from transitivity. The construction of the representative and the reduction to the ring are the content. H2.
